dedupe_keys.name: frequency duration and damages of global floods 1985 2015 processed dartmouth flood observatory archive

description: This dataset is the processed version of the Dartmouth Flood Observatory global flood archive used by Najibi and Devineni (2018) in Earth System Dynamics to analyse recent trends in the frequency and duration of global floods. It gives large flood events from 1985 to 2015 in five tables for event start date, end date, latitude, longitude and damages, which together allow counts, durations and losses to be mapped and compared across regions and years. It was deposited by Nasser Najibi of the City College of New York on Harvard Dataverse, with the current version released in April 2023, and is downloadable as tab-separated files under CC0 1.0. The depositor states it is for research purposes only and asks users to cite the paper and the Dartmouth Flood Observatory; the observatory's raw data, by G. R. Brakenridge and A. J. Kettner, are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with commercial use by permission. Caveats: use is limited to research, the raw data licence is non-commercial, and the processed copy ends in 2015. It is useful for historical event frequency analysis, hazard exposure baselines and calibration of flood risk and resilience models; a related record is the Global Flood Database of MODIS flood extents built from the same event list.
